question: Is the existing focused-test and CI evidence sufficient for this exact-head coordination race, or should merge wait for a real held-lease Actions run?
rationale: The patch changes cross-workflow state handling, and static tests cannot fully demonstrate the concurrent lease and durable-queue behavior in GitHub Actions.

options.title: Require held-lease Actions proof
options.body: Capture a redacted real run showing the command defers successfully while the existing exact-head review and queue retry ownership remain intact before merging.

options.title: Accept focused coverage
options.body: Merge based on the passing focused coordination and workflow tests, accepting that the concurrency path has not been re-demonstrated in Actions.

recommendation.title: Require held-lease Actions proof
recommendation.body: Capture a redacted real run showing the command defers successfully while the existing exact-head review and queue retry ownership remain intact before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the most directly connected recent automation contributor in the available history and can supply the requested run evidence.
